ARABIC LANGUAGE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #19
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ARABIC LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Public Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Public Speaking.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Public Speaking.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Public Speaking.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Public Speaking.

2. When practising Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation.

3. When practising Phonological Awareness: Fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Phonological Awareness: Fluency.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Phonological Awareness: Fluency.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonological Awareness: Fluency.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Phonological Awareness: Fluency.

4. When practising Reading Aloud: Arabic Alphabet, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading Aloud: Arabic Alphabet.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading Aloud: Arabic Alphabet.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading Aloud: Arabic Alphabet.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading Aloud: Arabic Alphabet.

5. In ARABIC LANGUAGE, the best classroom habit is: (1 mark)
   A. Mix random languages with no purpose
   B. Practise listening, speaking, reading, and writing every day
   C. Only memorise without using the language
   D. Avoid speaking to classmates

6. When practising Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening.

7. When practising Imitative Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Imitative Speaking.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Imitative Speaking.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Imitative Speaking.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Imitative Speaking.

8. When practising Interactive Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Interactive Speaking.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive Speaking.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Interactive Speaking.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Interactive Speaking.

9. When practising Conversational Skills, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Conversational Skills.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Conversational Skills.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Conversational Skills.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Conversational Skills.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
10. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing: Handwriting and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

11. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing: Creative Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

12. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

13. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

MARKING SCHEME
====

1. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Public Speaking.

2. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation.

3. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonological Awareness: Fluency.

4. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading Aloud: Arabic Alphabet.

5. B — Practise listening, speaking, reading, and writing every day

6. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening.

7. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Imitative Speaking.

8. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive Speaking.

9. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Conversational Skills.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Guided Writing: Handwriting; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

12. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Guided Writing; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
